From 6bd8b4a92a901fae1a422e6f914801063c345e8d Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Xu Yang <xu.yang_2@nxp.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Jan 2026 13:11:07 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] pmdomain: imx8m-blk-ctrl: fix out-of-range access of
 bc->domains

Fix out-of-range access of bc->domains in imx8m_blk_ctrl_remove().

Fixes: 2684ac05a8c4 ("soc: imx: add i.MX8M blk-ctrl driver")
Cc: stable@kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Xu Yang <xu.yang_2@nxp.com>
Reviewed-by: Daniel Baluta <daniel.baluta@nxp.com>
Signed-off-by: Ulf Hansson <ulf.hansson@linaro.org>

diff --git a/drivers/pmdomain/imx/imx8m-blk-ctrl.c b/drivers/pmdomain/imx/imx8m-blk-ctrl.c
index 74bf4936991d..19e992d2ee3b 100644
--- a/drivers/pmdomain/imx/imx8m-blk-ctrl.c
+++ b/drivers/pmdomain/imx/imx8m-blk-ctrl.c
@@ -340,7 +340,7 @@ static void imx8m_blk_ctrl_remove(struct platform_device *pdev)
 
 	of_genpd_del_provider(pdev->dev.of_node);
 
-	for (i = 0; bc->onecell_data.num_domains; i++) {
+	for (i = 0; i < bc->onecell_data.num_domains; i++) {
 		struct imx8m_blk_ctrl_domain *domain = &bc->domains[i];
 
 		pm_genpd_remove(&domain->genpd);
-- 
2.34.1

The patch fixes a bug in the `imx8m_blk_ctrl_remove()` function within `drivers/pmdomain/imx/imx8m-blk-ctrl.c`. The original loop condition incorrectly omitted the increment variable check (`i <`), leading to an out-of-range access of the `bc->domains` array. The fix adds the missing `i <` to the loop condition, ensuring correct iteration over the number of domains specified by `bc->onecell_data.num_domains`. This change prevents undefined behavior and potential crashes during driver removal.

Here is the commit message:
pmdomain: imx8m-blk-ctrl: fix out-of-range access of
 bc->domains

Fix out-of-range access of bc->domains in imx8m_blk_ctrl_remove().

Fixes: 2684ac05a8c4 ("soc: imx: add i.MX8M blk-ctrl driver")
Cc: stable@kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Xu Yang <xu.yang_2@nxp.com>
Reviewed-by: Daniel Baluta <daniel.baluta@nxp.com>
Signed-off-by: Ulf Hansson <ulf.hansson@linaro.org>

Here is the root cause:
The loop condition in `imx8m_blk_ctrl_remove()` was incorrectly written as `for (i = 0; bc->onecell_data.num_domains; i++)`, which always evaluates to true (since `num_domains` is a positive integer), causing an infinite loop that accesses `bc->domains[i]` beyond the allocated array bounds. This results in out-of-range memory access and potential crashes when removing the device.

Here is the patch:
 
 static void imx8m_blk_ctrl_remove(struct platform_device *pdev)
 {
 	struct imx8m_blk_ctrl *bc = dev_get_drvdata(&pdev->dev);
 	int i;
 
 	of_genpd_del_provider(pdev->dev.of_node);
 
-	for (i = 0; bc->onecell_data.num_domains; i++) {
+	for (i = 0; i < bc->onecell_data.num_domains; i++) {
 		struct imx8m_blk_ctrl_domain *domain = &bc->domains[i];
 
 		pm_genpd_remove(&domain->genpd);
 		dev_pm_domain_detach(domain->power_dev, true);
 	}
 
 	dev_pm_genpd_remove_notifier(bc->bus_power_dev);
 
 	dev_pm_domain_detach(bc->bus_power_dev, true);
 }

This causes `bc->domains[i]` to be accessed with `i` increasing indefinitely, reading or writing memory beyond the allocated array and leading to out-of-range access and potential crashes.

Reason:
